subject: POC orchestration: kickoff roles, timing, and acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@opsly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 14:06:00 -0700
Subject: POC orchestration: kickoff roles, timing, and acceptance criteria

Hi Daniel — thanks again for a great conversation earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before kickoff: 

Summary of what Opsly needs:
- Validate Redwood end-to-end latency and cost for conversational routing at 5K monthly active users (projected peak concurrency ~12).
- Confirm privacy controls (VPC + audit logs) and retention policy for customer metadata during the pilot.
- Demonstrate integration with Opsly’s ingestion pipeline (Kafka topic: opsly-prompt) and a sample routing flow.

Suggested POC scope (90-day compact):
1) Week 0 — kickoff & infra prep (dev/prod staging namespaces, KMS exchange test)
2) Weeks 1–3 — integration sprint (connector + sample dataset ingestion, smoke tests)
3) Weeks 4–6 — load & latency tuning (concurrency profiling, batching config)
4) Weeks 7–10 — quality validation & regression checks (prompt sets + evals)
5) Week 12 — final readout & runbook handoff

Acceptance criteria (what success looks like):
- 99th percentile generation latency under 400ms for 512-token horizon on dedicated instance configuration we discussed.
- Average token cost <= $0.0009/token under expected traffic profile.
- All data paths covered by audit logs and KMS key exchange validated.
- Integration demo: Opsly can send a message to the Kafka topic and receive a routed response in staging without manual intervention.

Owners (proposed):
- Redwood project lead: Karhtik Iyer (me) — overall POC orchestration, infra & runbook
- Redwood integration engineer: Aditya Rao — connector + test harness
- Opsly technical lead: Daniel Park — dataset, access to Kafka, acceptance on business criteria

Next steps:
- Daniel to confirm kickoff date and provide staging credentials.
- Karhtik to share a short mutual action plan and an attached sprint calendar.

Attachments: opsly-poc-schedule.xlsx, redwood-multiaction-plan.docx

Thanks — I’ll block 45 minutes on Wed for a kickoff if that works.

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: POC orchestration: kickoff roles, timing, and acceptance criteria

Karthik — this looks good and thorough, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Kickoff timing: Wed Apr 21 at 10:00am PT works for Daniel & me; Opsly infra team will join for the first 30 minutes.
2) Data: we’ll provide a ~10K message anonymized dataset, plus a streaming topic with synthetic traffic for load tests.
3) Constraint: procurement needs a signed MSS with the dev-only POC addendum before we start - I’ve looped in opsly-sales and procurement separately.

We’re comfortable with the acceptance criteria but would like a slightly higher token-cost target if possible; can Redwood provide a quick cost-sensitivity note for the two batching profiles we discussed?

I’ll confirm procurement timeline by end of day Tuesday. Kickoff invite appreciated.

—Daniel
Daniel Park
Director, Platform Engineering | Opsly
daniel.park@opsly.com

Thanks Daniel — confirmed for Wed Apr 21 10:00am PT. I attached a compact mutual action plan and a sprint calendar (opsly-poc-schedule.xlsx) — quick highlights and owner commitments below so everyone arrives ready: 

Immediate pre-kickoff checklist (owners):
- Procurement: Opsly procurement to return signed POC addendum (Daniel) — blocker for environment provisioning.
- Staging credentials: Opsly to share a service account with access to test Kafka topic (Daniel).
- Infra prep: Redwood to provision staging namespace + load generator (Karthik).
- Connector repo access: Opsly to add Aditya to the repo and provide sample schema (Daniel).

Weekly cadence and check-ins:
- Weekly engineering syncs (30 min) — Wednesdays 10:30am PT, internal action owners only.
- Joint demo sessions (60 min) — biweekly, show integration progress & metrics.
- Triage channel: #opsly-poc (Redwood Slack) — for daily async notes and blockers.

Reporting & artifacts:
- We’ll publish a short readout deck at week 6 and final runbook at week 12.
- Performance artifacts: token-cost runbook, latency breakdown, KV-cache hit-rate charts.

I dropped the two batching profile sensitivity scenarios in the attached sheet — early read: profile B (aggressive batching) saves ~18% in token cost but increases 95th p99 latency ~60ms for the workloads we sampled. We’ll tune during weeks 4–6 and present the trade-offs in the Week 6 readout.

If procurement returns the addendum by Tue EOD, we’ll be ready to run the infra prep tomorrow evening and have a green staging environment by Wednesday morning.

Attachments: opsly-poc-schedule.xlsx, redwood-multiaction-plan.docx

Regards,
Karthik
